1. Open Region and verify that United Kingdom and United States are available.
2. Select the region assigned to QA_REG_REGION_01 and read the notice below Region.
3. Complete the required fields, create the account, verify its email and sign in.
4. Open Settings > User Profile and inspect the account region.
expected:
1. Region provides United Kingdom and United States.
2. The notice reads: This sets where your health data is stored. It can't be changed later, so choose carefully.
3. Registration and verification retain the selected region.
4. User Profile shows the same region and provides no control that changes it.
evidence: Region options and notice, selected value, verification and User Profile region; execution record.

title: Apply glucose unit from the registration region

1. Register and verify one account with United Kingdom selected, then sign in and open Profile Setup.
2. Record the Country and Glucose unit.
3. Repeat with a fresh account and United States selected.

expected:
1. The hosted registration form uses Region and does not show a separate glucose-unit field.
2. Each account's Profile Setup shows the Country and unit defined for its registered region in Test Data.
3. The user cannot create a Country/Glucose unit mismatch after registration.
evidence: Both registration regions and both Profile Setup unit results; execution record.

title: Registration language and region mismatch warning

2. Select the incompatible Region and complete the other required fields.
3. Select Create an account and use the correction action on the mismatch warning.
4. Repeat the mismatch and use the continue action.
expected:
1. The form uses the selected language and region.
2. Before registration completes, a warning explains that signed-in content is unavailable in the selected language for that region.
3. The correction action returns to registration so the language or region can be changed.
4. The continue action allows registration to proceed. If no warning appears, record the case as failed.
evidence: Mismatch warning, correction path and continue path; execution record.

title: Reset password format validation
preconditions: A valid reset link has opened Update password.
procedure:
1. Enter matching values shorter than 12 characters that otherwise contain a number, lowercase letter, uppercase letter and special character.
2. Repeat with at least 12 characters while omitting, one at a time, the number, lowercase letter, uppercase letter and special character.
3. Enter matching values of at least 12 characters containing every required character type. Do not submit the valid password in this case.
expected:
1. Keycloak shows Invalid password: minimum length 12.
2. Keycloak shows the corresponding numerical digit, lower case, upper case or special character message for each omitted type.
3. No password-format message is shown for the valid-format value.
evidence: Each password-format message and valid-format state; execution record.

2. The expired link cannot open a usable Update password action and shows an expired or invalid-link state.
3. A new request is accepted and a new reset email arrives.
evidence: Reset-email timing, expired-link state and replacement email; execution record.

The TD-01.1-.3 account is signed in and onboarding has reached the Allow Bluetooth screen. Test data (QA Workbook): TD-01.1-.3, TD-53.2+.3, TD-59.1.
procedure:
1. Tap Allow on the Allow Bluetooth screen.
2. Tap Allow in the system permission prompt.
3. Continue through onboarding until the permission summary (You're all set) screen is displayed.
4. Open the TD-53.2+.3 OS permission path for Bluetooth/Nearby devices.
expected:
1. The system permission prompt opens.
2. The prompt closes and CGMx 1 moves to the next onboarding step (record its title) without showing the Bluetooth prompt again.
3. The permission summary shows Bluetooth as Allowed.
4. The OS shows Bluetooth/Nearby devices allowed for CGMx 1.
evidence: prompt screenshot; next-step screenshot; permission summary screenshot; OS permission screenshot; execution record.

title: Permission denied
preconditions: CGMx 1 has been freshly installed using the TD-59.1 method so Bluetooth/Nearby devices permission has never been requested ("not asked" state). Phone Bluetooth is ON. The TD-01.1-.3 account is signed in and onboarding has reached the Allow Bluetooth screen. Test data (QA Workbook): TD-01.1-.3, TD-53.2-.4, TD-59.1.
procedure:
1. Tap Allow on the Allow Bluetooth screen.
2. Tap Don't Allow (iOS) / Don't allow (Android) in the system permission prompt.
3. Open the TD-53.2+.3 OS permission path for Bluetooth/Nearby devices.
expected:
1. The system permission prompt opens.
2. The prompt closes without a crash; CGMx 1 displays guidance that Bluetooth permission is required together with a control that opens the phone settings for CGMx 1 (TD-53.4 label), and does not show Bluetooth as allowed.
3. The OS shows Bluetooth/Nearby devices not allowed for CGMx 1.
evidence: denial screenshot; in-app guidance/settings-link screenshot; OS permission screenshot; execution record.

title: Bluetooth hardware off
preconditions: Bluetooth/Nearby devices permission is allowed for CGMx 1. Onboarding has reached the Allow Bluetooth screen (or the next Bluetooth-dependent onboarding screen).
procedure:
1. Switch phone Bluetooth OFF from Control Centre (iOS) / Quick Settings (Android).
2. Tap Allow / Continue on the current onboarding screen.
3. Switch phone Bluetooth ON from Control Centre / Quick Settings.
4. Tap Allow / Continue again.
expected:
1. Phone Bluetooth is off.
2. CGMx 1 shows that Bluetooth is turned off and provides a way to turn it on (Android: system quick-enable prompt or in-app guidance; iOS: in-app guidance), and does not start transmitter scanning.
3. Phone Bluetooth is on.
4. CGMx 1 continues to the next onboarding step (record its title).
evidence: Bluetooth-off app screenshot; Bluetooth-on continuation screenshot; execution record.

title: Critical Alerts / DND onboarding screens and controls
preconditions: Notification permission is allowed. Onboarding has reached the first critical-alarm configuration screen (iOS: Critical Alerts; Android: Do Not Disturb access). Critical-alarm permissions have not been requested (fresh install per TD-59.1). Test data (QA Workbook): TD-59.1.
procedure:
1. Scroll each critical-alarm configuration screen from top to bottom before tapping its action button.
2. Tap the action button on each screen, answer any system prompt with Allow, and continue to the next screen until the critical-alarm configuration screens end.
expected:
1. Each screen explains the phone setting needed for critical alarms (notifications, critical alerts / Do Not Disturb, Bluetooth, and on Android auto-boot and battery optimisation) and warns that OS features creating separate "spaces" (e.g. iOS Work Focus, Android work profile / Private Space) can make alarms ineffective.
2. Each screen provides a direct action that opens the matching system prompt or settings page.
evidence: screenshot of each critical-alarm configuration screen and its action result; execution record.

title: Permission request and grant recognition

section: Platform Health Integration (Apple Health / Google Health)
title: Health access can be declined in onboarding and re-requested later from Settings
requirement:
DI-778 → DO-796
Android Health Connect: DO-794 / DO-795 / DO-796 are recorded as not implemented on Android; RA decision 2026-09-24 (item 20): missing feature = Fail.
preconditions: CGMx 1 has been freshly installed using the TD-59.1 reset/reinstall method, so Health access has never been allowed or refused on this phone. The TD-01.1-.3 account is signed in and first-use onboarding has reached the platform-health step (iOS: Step 01/15 Apple Health; Android: the Google Health / Health Connect step recorded in TD-47.7). If Home is shown after sign-in and the platform-health step is not presented, mark the case B, write the screen shown, and continue with the next case. Android: if the build under test has no Health Connect step, mark the Android run F (a missing feature is Fail, not B). Test data (QA Workbook): TD-01.1-.3, TD-47.6+.7 (Settings permission-management path), TD-59.1.
procedure:
1. Tap the platform-health permission button (TD-47.6 label).
2. In the system Health dialog tap Don't Allow (iOS) / Cancel or Don't allow (Android Health Connect).
3. Complete the remaining onboarding steps until Home is displayed.
4. Open the menu, go to the Settings permission-management path recorded in TD-47.6+.7 and tap the Apple Health / Google Health permission entry.
expected:
1. The system HealthKit (iOS) / Health Connect (Android) permission dialog opens once.
2. The dialog closes and onboarding moves to the next step without an error or a forced retry.
3. Onboarding completes and Home is displayed with glucose information.
4. CGMx 1 opens the system Health permission dialog again, or opens the CGMx 1 entry in phone Settings / the Health permission manager, where access can be allowed.
evidence: system dialog screenshot; next onboarding step screenshot; Home screenshot; Settings re-request screenshot; execution record.

title: Multiple simultaneous alarms preserve priority and do not suppress each other
preconditions: Onboarding is complete; Home shows an active sensor session receiving readings (QA_ACTIVE_01); notifications and critical-alarm prerequisites (iOS Critical Alerts; Android Do Not Disturb access) are allowed. 2. The Critical Low alarm remains shown on top; the no-data alarm is also active.
3. The Critical Low alarm is acknowledged; the critical no-data alarm remains active and is then shown.
4. Both alarms are acknowledged; neither was cleared by acknowledging the other.
evidence: recording of overlapping alarms and each acknowledgement; execution record.

day: Day 9 (= D0; TIR-001, TAR-002, TBR-002 between 14:00 and 17:59)
title: Break Day graph across a manually created real-device data gap
preconditions: A physical sensor/transmitter session is active and producing normal readings. Controlled Test Data records the test-account alias, sensor/transmitter/session identifier, expected reading frequency, approved out-of-range interruption method and intended interruption start time. Use one of these acceptance paths: (A) at least five consecutive measurement indexes remain missing after reconnection and are not backfilled; or (B) the timestamps surrounding the gap are more than 30 minutes apart. Record the last valid reading value/time/index before interruption and the first valid reading value/time/index after reconnection. No backend reading is created, deleted or changed for this case.
procedure:
1. Wait for a normal reading and record its value, timestamp, session identifier and measurement index where available.
2. Move the phone outside reliable Bluetooth range using the approved normal-device method.
3. Keep reception interrupted for at least five expected reading intervals.
4. Restore communication and wait for the first valid reading after reconnection.
5. Record its value, timestamp, session identifier and measurement index where available.
6. Confirm whether the expected measurement indexes remain missing or were backfilled.
7. If readings were backfilled or missing indexes cannot be demonstrated, repeat with an interruption that produces a time gap exceeding 30 minutes.
8. Open Reports > Day, navigate to the documented date and locate the interruption.
9. Inspect the glucose line immediately before, across and after the interval.
expected:
1. Valid readings exist before and after the interruption.
2. Either at least five consecutive measurement indexes remain missing, or the timestamps surrounding the gap are more than 30 minutes apart.
3. The Day graph contains a visible line break across the documented discontinuity.
4. The graph does not interpolate or imply a continuous glucose trend across the interval.
5. Normal graphing resumes when valid readings resume. If the five missed readings are backfilled and no greater-than-30-minute gap is produced, record the attempt as unsuitable test data rather than Pass.
evidence: Controlled Test Data record; reading before interruption; interruption start/end times and method; missing-index evidence or timestamps proving a gap exceeding 30 minutes; first reading after reconnection; Day graph screenshot; execution record.

day: Day 9 (= D0; TIR-001, TAR-002, TBR-002 between 14:00 and 17:59)
title: Recalculate Time in Range after changing a glucose threshold
preconditions: QA_TIR_01 is signed in; execute on D0 14:00-17:59. Its 200 mg/dL readings lie above the default High 10.0 mmol/L / 180 mg/dL (High is the default).
procedure:
1. Tap Reports > Time in Range on 7 Days and take a screenshot of all bands.
2. Open Settings > Reminder Settings, set High to the alternative High for the account unit (mmol/L account: 12.0 mmol/L; mg/dL account: 220 mg/dL) and tap Save settings.
3. Tap Reports > Time in Range on the same window and take a screenshot.
4. Restore High to 10.0 mmol/L / 180 mg/dL and tap Save settings.
expected:
1. Band values recorded.
2. The new High threshold is saved.
3. High band falls to 0% (0 h 0 min) and In Range increases by the former High readings; the displayed High threshold label shows the alternative High.
4. The original threshold is restored.
evidence: before/after screenshots; execution record.
